headline: New cells bring back sight in mice

sources.title: Blind People Offered Hope of Seeing Again After Stem Cell Breakthrough Remakes Retinal Blood Vessels (Good News Network)
Researchers Grow Rare Eye Vessel Cells to Halt Vision Loss (Neuroscience News)
Lab-Grown Retinal Cells Show Promise for New Eye Therapies (Duke Pratt School of Engineering)

chunks.text: Scientists at Duke University said they had {{carried out}} an [[exciting]] experiment. A team led by Professor Sharon Gerecht {{set out}} to grow tiny blood vessels for the [[retina]] using [[stem cells]]. These special cells are very hard to make, but the scientists {{came up with}} a [[clever]] way to grow them in the lab. Their [[goal]] was to help people who are slowly [[losing their sight]].

verbs.wrong: To repeat an experiment to check the results
verbs.correct: To do or perform a task or experiment
verbs.why: Scientists carry out experiments, and companies carry out surveys before launching a product. The Duke University team carried out a study on growing new blood vessel cells for the eye.

verbs.wrong: To promise to finish something important
verbs.correct: To begin a task with a clear goal
verbs.why: Explorers set out on long journeys, and researchers set out to answer a hard question. The Duke team set out to grow the delicate blood vessels found in the retina.

verbs.wrong: To copy a method from another team
verbs.correct: To think of a new idea or plan
verbs.why: Inventors come up with new gadgets, and cooks come up with recipes using leftovers. The scientists came up with a clever way to grow cells that are normally very hard to produce.

chunks.text: The researchers used stem cells that can [[turn into]] almost any cell in the body. In the lab, these cells slowly grew into the [[tissue]] that [[lines]] the blood vessels in the eye. To copy eye disease, the team put the tissue [[under stress]], and it started to {{break down}} [[in the same way]] it does in sick patients. These blood vessel tissue cells normally come only from inside the body, so growing them outside the body in the lab was a real [[breakthrough]].

verbs.why: Old cars break down on the highway, and a diet plan can break down after a few weeks. Under stress, the lab grown eye tissue broke down the same way it does in sick patients.

chunks.text: Next, the team tested the new cells in mice, not in people. They [[injected]] the cells into mice with weak, [[damaged]] eyes. The cells joined the tissue and {{built up}} strong, healthy blood vessels. This slowly {{brought the animals' sight back}}, and their [[vision]] got better. Mice that were treated early did not {{end up}} completely [[blind]].

verbs.wrong: To replace old cells with donor tissue
verbs.why: Regular training builds up muscle, and steady saving builds up a bank account over time. Inside the treated mice, the new cells built up strong, healthy blood vessels.

verbs.wrong: To start talking about a topic
verbs.why: A good night's sleep can bring back energy, and physical therapy can bring back lost movement. In the treated mice, the new cells slowly brought back some of their lost vision.

verbs.wrong: To stay the same without any change
verbs.correct: To finally be in a situation or place
verbs.why: Travelers end up lost without a map, and careless spenders end up broke by the end of the month. Mice that were treated early did not end up completely blind.

chunks.text: Professor Gerecht said the results [[point to]] a [[hopeful]] future, but she was [[careful]]. [[So far]] the [[method]] has only been tested in mice, so scientists cannot say yet that it will work in humans. They still need to work on safety before any tests in people. Doctors do not {{rule out}} problems, and they say a real [[treatment]] for [[diabetic retinopathy]], [[a leading cause]] of [[blindness]], may still be many [[years away]].

verbs.wrong: To warn people about a possible danger
verbs.correct: To decide that something is not possible
verbs.why: Doctors rule out serious illness with tests, and mechanics rule out engine trouble first. Researchers do not rule out safety problems before any human trials can begin.

mainIdea.s: A team at Duke University set out to grow blood vessel cells for the eye using stem cells. When they tested the cells in mice with damaged eyes, some vision came back.
mainIdea.why: The scientists grew the blood vessel cells from stem cells and tested them in mice with damaged eyes. The mice slowly got some of their vision back.

mainIdea.s: Scientists at Duke University used cells taken from healthy human donors to fix mice with damaged eyes. They say the treatment is now ready to help blind people see again.
mainIdea.why: Close, but the cells did not come from human donors, they were grown in the lab from stem cells. The article says a human treatment is still years away.

mainIdea.s: Doctors are running new trials of a laser treatment for diabetic retinopathy in older adult patients. Early results show the therapy slows vision loss without any surgery.
mainIdea.why: This story is about mice regaining sight after a stem cell experiment at Duke University. It is not about a laser treatment trial for older patients.

tf.s: The scientists came up with a new way to grow the special cells in the lab.
tf.why: They came up with (thought of) a clever new way to grow the cells, so this is true.

tf.s: In the lab, the stem cells broke down before they could form new tissue.
tf.why: The stem cells grew into the tissue that lines blood vessels (they developed into it). Break down means to fall apart or stop working, which is not what happened.

tf.s: The new cells brought back vision in many of the treated mice.
tf.why: The cells brought back the mice's vision (made it return), which really happened in the study.

tf.s: Professor Gerecht said the results rule out a hopeful future.
tf.why: The results point to a hopeful future (they suggest good things are likely). Rule out means to say something is not possible, the opposite of what she meant.

tf.s: In the treated mice, the cells broke down the eye's blood vessels.
tf.why: The cells built up strong new blood vessels (made them grow stronger). Break down means to make something fall apart, the opposite of what the cells did.

tf.s: The scientists carried out their eye experiment at Duke University.
tf.why: They did carry out (perform) the experiment at Duke University, so this is true.
